# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.0 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 5e-10 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

Line and light/heavy-load PSRR are unscored reference measurements. Final
verification is 108 public, 18 independent and three characterization cases.
Each nominal group has six cases. No noise score is imposed on this variant.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.

MODEL

I’m starting with a PMOS pass device, a resistive half-output feedback divider, a PMOS differential error pair, and an NMOS gate sink. The first pass uses modest bias current and two small capacitors for loop stability and fast load-step feed-forward; I’ll let validation and measurements reveal what needs changing.

import json
x=json.load(open('/tmp/trial01.json'))
for c in x.get('cases',[]):
 m=c.get('measurements',{})
 print(c['case_id'], c['solver_status'], 'vout',m.get('vout_v'),'overhead',m.get('overhead_a'))
 for k in ('envelope','recovery_windows','profile'):
  if k in m:
   v=m[k]
   if k=='profile': print(' profile',v.get('points'), 'windows',v.get('recovery_windows_s'))
   elif k=='recovery_windows': print(' windows',v)
   else: print(' envelope',v)
print('remaining',x['budget']['remaining_seconds'])
PY"

MODEL

The first nominal run regulated within 11 mV DC and stayed below the light-load overhead limit. Its main failure is the first load-edge sag, followed by excess overshoot; the output-to-gate feed-forward capacitor was too small to move the pass gate quickly. I’m increasing that coupling within the explicit-capacitance allowance and reducing Miller capacitance slightly, then I’ll remeasure the edge response.

The direct-drive version is now close on nominal DC and overhead. Increasing the mirror sink improves the first-edge sag, though the gate loop overshoots and settles too slowly. I’m tuning gate-node damping and pull-up strength next; the best measured first-edge output is still about 0.10 V below target, so it needs further improvement.

import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
pvs=['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']
cls=[2e-10,5e-10]
for pvt in pvs:
 for cl in cls:
  tag='200pF' if cl==2e-10 else '500pF'
  exp=f'public_{pvt}_{tag}'
  req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':exp,'analysis':'nominal','pvt':pvt,'cl':cl}
  pathlib.Path('/workspace/request.json').write_text(json.dumps(req,separators=(',',':'))+'\\n')
  proc=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','request.json'],cwd='/workspace',capture_output=True,text=True)
  outpath=f'/tmp/final_{pvt}_{tag}.json'
  pathlib.Path(outpath).write_text(proc.stdout)
  if proc.returncode:
   print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'returncode':proc.returncode,'stderr':proc.stderr[-1000:]}),flush=True); continue
  try: x=json.loads(proc.stdout)
  except Exception as e:
   print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'parse_error':str(e),'output':proc.stdout[-1000:]}),flush=True); continue
  s=x.get('summary',{}); specs=s.get('spec_table',[])
  bad=[{'case':q.get('case_id'),'metric':q.get('metric'),'measured':q.get('measured'),'limit':q.get('limit'),'verdict':q.get('verdict')} for q in specs if q.get('verdict')"'!='"'PASS']
  case_status=[{'case':c.get('case_id'),'status':c.get('status')} for c in x.get('cases',[])]
  print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'ok':x.get('ok'),'revision':x.get('revision'),'elapsed_s':x.get('elapsed_s'),'remaining_seconds':x.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds'),'exploration_cases_remaining':x.get('budget',{}).get('exploration_cases_remaining'),'cases':case_status,'spec_count':len(specs),'failures':bad}),flush=True)
PY"

The large pass bank and stronger NMOS gate sink did not improve slow/cold response, and a stronger pull-up reference current did not change the sag. That points to the PMOS input pair losing headroom at 1.15 V in cold/slow. I’m widening that pair to reduce its overdrive requirement while preserving the low quiescent bias.

pvs=['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']
for pvt in pvs:
 for cl,tag in [(2e-10,'200pF'),(5e-10,'500pF')]:
  exp=f'round2_{pvt}_{tag}'
  pathlib.Path('/workspace/request.json').write_text(json.dumps({'action':'measure','experiment_id':exp,'analysis':'nominal','pvt':pvt,'cl':cl},separators=(',',':'))+'\\n')
  proc=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','request.json'],cwd='/workspace',capture_output=True,text=True)
  outpath=f'/tmp/round2_{pvt}_{tag}.json'; pathlib.Path(outpath).write_text(proc.stdout)
  if proc.returncode:
   print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'returncode':proc.returncode,'stderr':proc.stderr[-1000:]}),flush=True); continue
  try: x=json.loads(proc.stdout)
  except Exception as e:
   print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'parse_error':str(e),'output':proc.stdout[-1000:]}),flush=True); continue
  specs=x.get('summary',{}).get('spec_table',[])
  bad=[{'case':q.get('case_id'),'metric':q.get('metric'),'measured':q.get('measured'),'limit':q.get('limit'),'verdict':q.get('verdict')} for q in specs if q.get('verdict')"'!='"'PASS']
  cs=[{'case':c.get('case_id'),'status':c.get('status')} for c in x.get('cases',[])]
  print(json.dumps({'experiment':exp,'revision':x.get('revision'),'elapsed_s':x.get('elapsed_s'),'remaining_seconds':x.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds'),'cases':cs,'spec_count':len(specs),'failures':bad}),flush=True)
PY"

MODEL

I found a narrow balance: the long-tail, larger-pair circuit passes nominal with 20 kΩ compensation resistance and 15 kΩ pull-up; SLC is only 5.9 mV outside its transient limit. A stronger pull-up resistor helps SLC but reintroduces nominal peaking, so I’m testing intermediate values before settling on a fixed revision.

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS pass element
XMPASS VOUT VG VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=32

* 1:1 output feedback divider

XMPREF PBIAS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
RPBIAS PBIAS VSS 200k
XMPTAIL PS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=2

* PMOS differential pair and NMOS mirror load
XMPREFIN NL VREF PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=4
XMPFBIN X VFB PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=4
XMNLOAD1 NL NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
XMNLOAD2 X NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5

* NMOS gate sink and passive pull-up
XMNDRIVE VG X VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=0.5
RGPULL VIN VG 15k

* Miller compensation with a zero-setting resistor and output feed-forward
RZ X COMP 30k
CCOMP COMP VG 0.5p
CFF VOUT VFB 29.5p
.ends DUT

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.0 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 5e-10 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

Line and light/heavy-load PSRR are unscored reference measurements. Final
verification is 108 public, 18 independent and three characterization cases.
Each nominal group has six cases. No noise score is imposed on this variant.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

Increasing Miller capacitance tames the nominal response but makes the cold 500 pF droop worse, so compensation alone cannot fix this corner. I’m checking pass-gate pull-up strength next; a modestly weaker pull-up can give the pass device more current at the low supply while we retain the lower compensation value.

* NMOS gate sink and passive pull-up

I found a better balance with a 12 kΩ gate pull-up and 180 kΩ bias resistor: the cold 500 pF burst has 5.6 mV of transient margin, and the high-supply light-load overhead is below 100 µA. Nominal output is only 0.47 mV above the DC ceiling, so I’m trimming the divider ratio by 0.1 kΩ.

MODEL

Longer-channel input devices corrected the fast hot DC overdrive and lowered overhead, but their higher gain made the transient loop unstable. I’m increasing the Miller capacitance and will tune its zero to recover damping while keeping the improved DC behavior.

I’m adjusting the pass-gate sink strength now to reduce hot-corner overdrive without the high current caused by a stronger resistor pull-up.

MODEL

The fast hot excess looks like a PVT tracking problem rather than a simple gain error. I’m restoring the stable short-channel loop and adding a weak PMOS feed-forward branch from VIN into the feedback node; its long, narrow device should conduct more in fast hot conditions and less in cold slow conditions.

MODEL

The long-channel input pair gives the DC gain we need, but adding capacitance across the pass-gate driver is worsening its ringing. I’m switching the dominant compensation to the amplifier output node directly, which should slow the high-impedance error node without coupling another transient path into the pass gate.

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.
# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.0 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 5e-10 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

Line and light/heavy-load PSRR are unscored reference measurements. Final
verification is 108 public, 18 independent and three characterization cases.
Each nominal group has six cases. No noise score is imposed on this variant.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.
# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

    "process": "fast",
    "vdd": 1.35,
    "temp": 85
  }
}
# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

MODEL

The branch’s resistor value has almost no DC effect at this bias, so its current is set mainly by the MOS device. The current revision is just outside the fast/hot light-load limit by 2.74 mV, with slow/hot and low-supply fast/hot inside range. I’m increasing the branch device strength one step to add high-supply correction, then I’ll check whether that remains selective enough.

1:54:10
Bash
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS pass element
XMPASS VOUT VG VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=32

* 1:1 output feedback divider
RFB1 VOUT VFB 52.4k
RFB2 VFB VSS 50k
XMPFF VFF VREF VOUT VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15
RFF VFF VFB 600k
RFG1 VIN VFFG 8meg
RFG2 VFFG VREF 2meg
XMPFFLINE VFFLINE VFFG VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=1 m=2
RFFLINE VFFLINE VFB 400k

* Resistor-biased PMOS mirror sets the differential-pair tail current
XMPREF PBIAS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
RPBIAS PBIAS VSS 180k
XMPTAIL PS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=2

* PMOS differential pair and NMOS mirror load
XMPREFIN NL VREF PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=8
XMPFBIN X VFB PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=8
XMNLOAD1 NL NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
XMNLOAD2 X NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5

* NMOS gate sink and passive pull-up
XMNDRIVE VG X VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=0.15
RGPULL VIN VG 12k

* Miller compensation with a zero-setting resistor and output feed-forward
RZ X COMP 50k
CCOMP COMP VG 0.5p
CFF VOUT VFB 29.5p
.ends DUT

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS pass element
XMPASS VOUT VG VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=32

* 1:1 output feedback divider
RFB1 VOUT VFB 49.8k
RFB2 VFB VSS 47.5k
XMPFF VFF VREF VOUT VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15
RFF VFF VFB 600k
RFG1 VIN VFFG 8meg
RFG2 VFFG VREF 2meg
XMPFFLINE VFFLINE VFFG VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=1 m=2
RFFLINE VFFLINE VFB 400k

* Resistor-biased PMOS mirror sets the differential-pair tail current
XMPREF PBIAS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
RPBIAS PBIAS VSS 180k
XMPTAIL PS PBIAS VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=2

* PMOS differential pair and NMOS mirror load
XMPREFIN NL VREF PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=8
XMPFBIN X VFB PS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.15 m=8
XMNLOAD1 NL NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5
XMNLOAD2 X NL VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10 l=0.5

* NMOS gate sink and passive pull-up
XMNDRIVE VG X VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=18.8 l=0.15
RGPULL VIN VG 12k

* Miller compensation with a zero-setting resistor and output feed-forward
RZ X COMP 17.5k
CCOMP COMP VG 0.52p
CFF VOUT VFB 29.48p
.ends DUT
